_doc: ONE framing entry per asset, used on EVERY screen that shows it (docs/TRUTH.md 'Framing data'; editor: docs/tools/FRAMING_TOOL.md).
Sections: heroes / enemies / bosses (portraits, keyed by portrait file basename without .png) and items / relics (keyed by item or relic id).
All pixel values are SOURCE pixels of the PNG as it sits on disk (before the enemy mirror and before any runtime content crop). Source images are never modified.

Portrait fields: head_top = topmost pixel of the SKULL/HELMET DOME only (never antennas, hoods, horns, crowns, halos, glow); chin = bottom of the head; center_x = the head's horizontal centre. Hand-declared by Kev — NEVER derived from pixels (the 2026-07-12 framing failure).
use_anchors: true makes PixelUI.cover_fit_portrait frame the asset from head_top/chin/center_x against _targets[section]; absent/false keeps the pre-anchor look (legacy_* fields apply).

legacy_zoom (x cover scale), legacy_anchor_y (fraction of frame height, + = art up), legacy_down_px (final-display px, + = art down): pre-anchor per-asset offsets migrated out of code; ignored once use_anchors is true.

Item/relic fields: center_x/center_y = the art's visual centre (placed at the box centre), scale = multiplier on each screen's fit (integer-law screens round to a whole multiple). Consumed by PixelUI.fit_item_art.

insets {left,top,right,bottom}: source pixels trimmed off each edge (stray neighbouring-sprite fragments). stray: 'rejected' dismisses a stray-pixel scan flag. reviewed: Kev has checked this asset in the framing editor.
_crop_tool is the offline scripts/assets/portrait_frame_crop.py preview config (heroes only). Its old 'apply' mode is retired: the runtime anchor fit replaces the destructive crop pass.
